Author: Umesh A. Trivedi

DATED: 20/02/2023  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION NO. 2517 of 2023 ==========================================================
 DHIRJIBHAI MAHADEVBHAI DESAI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
MR MJ MEHTA(5797) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR SAURABH J MEHTA(2170) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR DHAWAN JAYSWAL APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 MR HAVEWALLA for Respondent No.2 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE UMESH A. TRIVEDI  Date : 20/02/2023  ORAL ORDER 1. Mr.Havewalla, learned advocate has instructions to appear on behalf of first informant.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Registry is hereby directed to accept the appearance that may be filed by the first informant.
3. Rule returnable forthwith.

4. Mr.Dhawan Jayswal, learned APP waives service of rule on behalf of Respondent-State and Mr.Havewalla, learned advocate waives service of rule on behalf of first informant i.e. Respondent No.2.
5.

The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection R/CR.MA/2517/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/02/2023 with FIR being No.11217026220596 of 2022 registered with Patan Taluka Police Station, Patan for offence under Dhirjibhai Mahadevbhai Desai vs State Of Gujarat on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166896434/
1 Sections 420, 406, 389 and 506(1) of the Indian Penal Code, prior to submission of charge-sheet.
6.

entities.text: Dhirjibhai Mahadevbhai Desai vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
7. Learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
8. Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

9. Mr.Saurabh Mehta, learned advocate for the applicant submitted that though the allegations levelled in the FIR are not correct as transaction in between the applicant and the first informant is purely civil transaction and instead of invoking civil remedy, present FIR is filed, he has shown his willingness to return back the amount obtained as earnest money out of the transaction for which Mr.Rabari Labhubhai Shambhubhai who happens to be brother-in-law of applicant, namely,
Dhirjibhai Mahadevbhai Desai has filed undertaking before the Court.
The applicant-accused will pay monthly installment of Rs.80,916/- and clear up the total amount within a period of 1 year from the date of release of the applicant - accused.

The details of the bank account provided by the complainant is also mentioned in the undertaking and he assures that the aforesaid amount will be R/CR.MA/2517/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/02/2023 paid by the applicant-accused directly in bank account of the complainant.
The undertaking further discloses that if the applicant -accused fails to pay 3 consequtive installment then the complainant herein will be at liberty to file an application for cancellation of bail.

He has further submitted that after the applicant- accused is released on bail, he shall file the same undertaking before this Court on line of this very undertaking filed by Rabari Labhubhai Shambhubhai.
10. Mr.Havewalla, learned advocate appearing for first informant submitted that he does not agree to the submission that the transaction for which FIR is filed reflects only civil transactions.

However, he has submitted that if the applicant- accused refunds the earnest money which was paid to him as per the undertaking filed by Rabari Labhubhai Shambhubhai and undertaking which is to be filed by the applicant-accused within a period of 1 week from his release from prison, he has no objection if applicant-accused is released on bail.

11. Mr.Dhawan Jayswal, learned APP submitted that if interest of both the applicant-accused as also first informant is protected, the Court may pass appropriate order releasing applicant on appropriate terms and conditions.

12. Having gone through the contents of the FIR as also impugned order and the undertaking filed by Rabari Labhubhai Shambhubhai, brother-in-law of the applicant-accused, Dhirjibhai Mahadevbhai Desai, I deem it fit to release the applicant - accused on bail pending trial.

R/CR.MA/2517/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/02/2023 Dhirjibhai Mahadevbhai Desai vs State Of Gujarat on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166896434/
2 13.

entities.text: Dhirjibhai Mahadevbhai Desai vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the present application is allowed.
If he fails to pay three (3) consecutive installments as mentioned in the undertaking voluntarily, the first informant is at liberty to pray for cancellation of bail.

However,
first three monthly installments has to be paid invariably without any excuses.
The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
15. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(UMESH A. TRIVEDI, J) ASHISH M. GADHIYA Dhirjibhai Mahadevbhai Desai vs State Of Gujarat on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166896434/
